text:
liam (sales): Heads-up — CascadeCorp wants a POC to swap CompetitorY endpoints to Redwood with identical search+extract UX. Top asks: adapter shim, token parity, sample pricing to match their bundle, and procurement security answers. nina can you own the tech checklist?

nina (solutions): Yep. Draft checklist: 1) request/response mapping doc 2) tokenizer sample run (200 prompts) 3) prompt normalization & stop-seq mapping 4) retry semantics & rate limits 5) parity harness + metrics 6) pricing scenarios to mirror bundle 7) procurement Qs answered.

ark (eng): Adapter is a tiny proxy that rewrites CompetitorY JSON to Redwood schema. We'll add a token-recount shim and explicit temperature/stop overrides. Quick example mapping: client POST /compy/v1/gen {"q":"...","max":300} -> adapter POST /v1/complete {"input":"...","max_total_tokens":300, "temperature":0.0, "stop":["\n\n"]}

sara (security): Procurement wants EU residency, KMS/HSM, audit logs, and IP allowlist. Short answers: EU pinning supported in Private/Dedicated, CMK via AWS KMS yes, HSM via partner (legal loop), audit logs exportable to S3. Send their highlighted questionnaire.

otto (sales-eng): Pricing note — CompetitorY sells 100k-call bundles. Options: 1) token-equivalent with measured delta 2) flat-call mapping using avg tokens per call 3) migration credit month. I'll calculate example invoices for 50k calls with a ~+11% token delta assumption.

mel (cs): Canary ops: run synthetic parity set first, then 5% live traffic with auto-failback to CompetitorY on >=2 errors/5m. Capture diffs (token delta, structured extraction mismatch, parsing errors) and output CSV for triage.

ark (eng): On response diffs — likely causes: tokenizer vocab, implicit temp, and stop handling. Mitigation: explicit temp/seed, explicit stop tokens, post-normalize whitespace. We'll add a small heuristic to trim trailing punctuation differences.

nina (solutions): I'll run the 200-prompt tokenization comparison and share results by EOD. If delta is consistent, propose a first-month migration credit or rate tweak.

sara (security): I'll draft procurement answers (EU residency confirmation, KMS details, log retention options) by tomorrow noon. Need the highlighted PDF.

liam (sales): I'll upload the questionnaire and mark three redlines. we need staging IPs by 08:30 tomorrow. ark can infra provide ephemeral /28?

ark (eng): Yes, will DM a /28 range and NAT details. Adapter logs will redact PII by default; configurable.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: compy-adapter -> canary-2026-04-05T09:00Z (5% traffic). CI checks: unit + parity-harness.

nina (solutions): Action items: 1) 200-prompt tokenizer run -> nina (EOD) 2) adapter stub & mapping doc -> ark (tomorrow 09:00) 3) procurement answers -> sara + legal (tomorrow noon) 4) pricing examples -> otto (tomorrow COB) 5) parity harness -> nina + ark (day 1 of POC) 6) canary runbook & failback -> mel (pre-canary).

liam (sales): Thanks team — 09:00 sync tomorrow quick 10m. Ping here if blocked. :thumbsup:
